newsitem.title: UK: Czech gas supply may be decided within weeks.
newsitem.headline: Czech gas supply may be decided within weeks.

text.p: The Czech Republic may be close to diversifying natural gas supplies away from Russia, deputy minister at the Ministry of Industry and Trade, Miroslav Tvrznik said on Monday.
"It could be solved in the next two or three weeks," said Tvrznik, who has special responsibility for energy affairs, adding that the issue would be resolved within a month at most.
This echoed Industry and Trade Minister Vladimir Dlouhy, who told reporters in Prague on Friday that a plan would be submitted to the cabinet within two weeks.

"The import of gas is more a political than an economic or energy problem", said Tvrznik. "It was first discussed in November last year. When I was leaving Prague I handed over the second phase of the documents to the minister and it will be discussed next week."
Tvrznik said the Republic aimed to diversify both the transport route of new gas supplies and the source.

"It was clear that there was no more space on the pipeline through Ukraine, the Slovak Republic and the Czech Republic," he said, adding that capacity was nine billion cubic metres a year, the same as current Czech consumption.
"So any additional gas must come through the western borders," Tvtznik said.
Norway, the Netherlands, Britain and Germany, were under consideration,although Tvrznik would not say which was favoured.
"But in any case, the extra molecules consumed will be Russian," he added.

He explained that if the Czech Republic buys gas from, for example, Norway, Norwegian gas would be moved to Germany and the Republic will then do a location exchange at its border to import Russian gas in exchange for the Norwegian supply.
As a result, no Norwegian or any other non-Russian supply will actually be consumed in the Czech republic.
